summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and GERD was admitted for substernal chest pain that improved with leaning forward and had a pleuritic component. Initial evaluation revealed sinus tachycardia, positional chest pain, and EKG changes including ST elevations in leads I and aVL, but normal troponins and echocardiogram. Pericarditis was diagnosed, likely due to a viral illness masked by immunosuppression. He was treated with colchicine and aspirin, avoiding NSAIDs due to transplant and kidney status. Volume overload from recent Lasix discontinuation was managed with diuresis. Symptoms resolved rapidly, and he was discharged home on colchicine for four weeks and restarted on Lasix, with follow-up planned for transplant and pancreatic cyst monitoring.
